options: A vector (list of numbers) that represents a token's or text's meaning
A compressed version of the original text's characters
A password used to access the model's API
The literal dictionary definition stored as text
questions.explain: An embedding is a learned vector of numbers — hundreds to thousands of dimensions — that represents meaning, not a text compression or a dictionary lookup.

questions.q: In embedding space, what does it mean for two tokens to be "close" to each other?
options: They are spelled similarly
They were typed at a similar time
Their vectors point in similar directions, reflecting similar meaning or usage
They are always synonyms with identical definitions
questions.explain: Closeness in embedding space reflects similar meaning or similar usage context — not spelling, and not necessarily a strict synonym relationship.

questions.q: What does the "king - man + woman ≈ queen" example demonstrate?
options: That embeddings can encode relationships between concepts, not just isolated word identity
That the model was explicitly programmed with gender and royalty rules
That embeddings only work for royalty-related words
That subtraction is not possible with vectors
questions.explain: This classic example shows that vector arithmetic on embeddings can capture real relationships (like gender) that emerged purely from patterns in training data, not explicit rules.

options: The literal character-by-character overlap between two strings
The angle between two vectors, used to measure how close their meanings are
How many tokens two pieces of text share
The file size of two embedding vectors
questions.explain: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two embedding vectors, typically ranging from -1 (opposite) to 1 (identical), independent of vector length.

questions.q: Which of these is a real-world use of embeddings outside of a chat model's internal attention mechanism?
options: Semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Compiling source code into a binary
Rendering images in a web browser
Encrypting network traffic
questions.explain: Embeddings are widely used standalone for semantic search, recommendations, and RAG — finding the nearest-matching content by meaning rather than exact keywords.
